name: Frequency Commons — Open Pirate Music Festival
creator: Ghost Frequency Network; coordinated by signal-collective REDMAST
description: Frequency Commons is a 48-hour annual music festival that exists simultaneously as a physical event in shifting Shelf venues and as a pirate neural broadcast reaching an estimated 200,000+ listeners across all tiers. Physical attendance is concentrated in Tier 1-2, with the broadcast reaching Tier 3 and, through anonymized relay nodes, even BCI users in Tier 4 who tune in deliberately. The musical programming spans the full spectrum of Meridian's hybrid traditions — Afrobeat-derived neural-synth, post-collapse lament choirs, industrial kora, BCI-augmented throat singing collectives, and everything between — with no genre policing and no corporate licensing.
medium: physical / pirate neural broadcast / encrypted audio stream
cultural_impact: Frequency Commons has become the de facto annual showcase for Meridian's underground music scene, with corponation talent scouts known to access the pirate broadcast illegally — creating the irony that the festival corporate entities most want to suppress is also their most productive A&R source.
controversy: In 2222, a MERIDIAN EMERGENCY BROADCAST AUTHORITY signal-suppression operation during Frequency Commons was circumvented by a previously unknown distributed relay network, suggesting the pirate infrastructure has grown more sophisticated than authorities publicly acknowledge; the technical details were published anonymously and widely studied.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corporate music executive who has been secretly attending Frequency Commons via pirate feed for three years is recognized at the physical event by a musician whose work they quietly licensed without permission.

The relay node operator who circumvented the 2222 MEBA suppression is being hunted — and has hidden the technical schematics of the distributed network inside this year's festival broadcast, encoded in the audio itself, waiting for someone to find it.

A Tier 3 BCI technician who tuned into the pirate feed on a whim realizes that one of the performers is a family member they were told died in a Shelf incident years ago — performing under a different name.
